subject: Eval sprint: credential orchestration, IP allowlist, and peering cadence
messages:
From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Hart <sam.hart@asterrahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Nov 2025 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Eval sprint kickoff — credentials, allowlist, peering (initial checklist)

Hi Sam,

Thanks again for committing time this week. To make the evaluation sprint smooth, I pulled together the initial checklist we discussed. High level asks below — we can pivot but want to lock the close path and responsibilities.

Key items for sprint start (week of Nov 10):
- Org setup: add Asterra as a tenant in our staging org (service account + admin contact).
- API keys: short-lived API key + service account token; we’ll provide rotation guidance.
- IP allowlist: we need a(final) list of outbound IPs from Asterra for peering and the sample CSV below.
- VPC peering: details for the dedicated peering request (CIDR, owner contact).

Attachments: I’m including a starter MAP spreadsheet (asterra_map_v1.xlsx) and a network_allowlist_template.csv to populate. Ben (cc’d) will own the peering packet with you — looping him in.

Request: can you confirm the internal contacts for networking and security and a preferred time for a 30-min Handoff call next week?

Thanks,
Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

Kim,

Appreciate the clear breakdown. We're aligned on the scope. Quick answers:
- Networking lead: Priya Desai (pri@asterrahealth.com).
- Security lead: security@asterrahealth.com (internal queue, I'll copy specific contact as needed).
- We can populate the allowlist CSV by EOD Monday (Nov 10).

Question: your API key plan — are you issuing short-lived keys per-service account or do you prefer we create a single service account that you mint tokens from? Our security team prefers minimal long-lived credentials.

30-min handoff window: Nov 11 at 10:30am PT works for our infra folks — does that fit on your side?

Thanks,
Sam

Subject: Re: Eval sprint kickoff — credentials, allowlist, peering (network/peering details)

Sam / Kim — thanks for the loop. Ben here from Solutions Engineering. I’ll own the peering packet and can draft the request during our handoff. A few practical notes before the call:

1) API approach: we recommend customer-managed service account (your preferred path). We will then mint ephemeral tokens scoped to evaluation endpoints; no long-lived keys stored on our side. That keeps you compliant and gives us a predictable rotation cadence.

2) IPs & CIDR: for VPC peering we need:
   - Customer VPC CIDR (e.g., 10.20.0.0/16)
   - Egress IPs that should be allowed to call Redwood (we provide a small set of egress NAT IPs; template attached).

3) Peering request: please attach a PDF or signed form with the network owner and a point-of-contact for ticket handoff. I attached a sample (vpc-peering-request.pdf).

I attached the network_allowlist_template.csv and included inline example rows. Sample: 35.209.112.5, 35.209.112.6

I’ll drop an agenda for Nov 11 10:30am PT in a calendar invite:
- 10 min: intro + responsibilities
- 10 min: API key flow + rotation plan
- 10 min: network peering steps + ticketing

--
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
From: Asterra Security <security@asterrahealth.com>

Date: Fri, 7 Nov 2025 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Eval sprint kickoff — credentials, allowlist, peering (security checklist)

Team,

Quick security requests ahead of the sprint:
- SOC 2 evidence: please provide the SOC 2 status and any relevant certs or audit reports.
- KMS / key management: describe whether Redwood will require customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for logs and model payloads during the trial or if your KMS integration is only for Private deployments.
- Data residency and retention: we need defaults for eval traces and logs and an opt-out path.

If you can include the SOC 2 summary in the Drive folder, that’ll help speed our internal signoff. Otherwise we will need an SLA exception for the eval window.

Thanks,
Asterra Security
security@asterrahealth.com

Subject: Re: Eval sprint kickoff — credentials, allowlist, peering (close timeline & next steps)

Great progress — thanks all. Recap and proposed close timeline:

Open items and owners
- Asterra: populate network_allowlist_template.csv (Sam / Priya) — due Nov 10 EOD.
- Asterra Security: confirm SOC 2 summary or indicate SLA exception needed — due Nov 10 EOD.
- Redwood (Ben): prepare VPC peering request packet and pre-fill details — due Nov 11 (post-handoff).
- Redwood (Kim): provision staging tenant and create service account stub for your infra team to validate — Nov 12 morning.

Target close path for evaluation sprint:
- Nov 11: Handoff call (10:30am PT) — confirm peering cadence and API token flow.
- Nov 12–13: Networking ticket submitted and API key validation.
- Nov 14: Smoke test (basic generate + small-chat) from Asterra staging to Redwood staging.
- Nov 18: Evaluation check-in and decisioning (customer feedback + next steps).

Attachments uploaded to shared Drive: asterra_map_v1.xlsx (MAP with milestones), network_allowlist_template.csv, vpc-peering-request.pdf.

If anything in the timeline looks tight, flag now and we’ll shift the smoke test window. Otherwise I’ll set the Nov 11 calendar invite and share the Drive link in the invite.

Best,
Kim
